title: On-Chip Octanol-Assisted Liposome Assembly for Bioengineering
protocol: Take a 4 inch diameter clean silicon wafer.
Clean it further using pressurized air to remove dust particles.
Mount the wafer on a spin coater.
Gently dispense approximately 5 mL of negative photoresist in the center of the wafer, avoiding air bubbles.
Spin-coat the wafer at 500 rpm for 30 seconds with an acceleration of 100 rpm/s for initial spreading.
Increase the speed to 3000 rpm and spin for 60 seconds with an acceleration of 500 rpm/s to achieve a 10 μm thick photoresist layer.
Bake the wafer on a heating plate at 65 °C for 2 minutes, then at 95 °C for 5 minutes.
Cool down the wafer.
Mount the wafer in the printing chamber of the direct-write optical lithography machine.
Feed the OLA design into the software.
Print the OLA design(s) on the coated wafer using a UV laser with a dose of 300 mJ/cm².
Bake the wafer at 65 °C for 1 min.
Bake the wafer at 95 °C for 3 min.
Dip the wafer in a glass beaker containing the developer solution until the uncured photoresist is fully removed.
Wash the wafer with acetone.
Wash the wafer with isopropanol.
Wash the wafer with deionized (DI) water.
Blow dry the wafer using pressurized air/N2.
Hard-bake the wafer at 150 °C for 30 min.
Place the master wafer on a square piece of aluminum.
Wrap the aluminum foil around the wafer to form a well-like structure.
Measure 40 g of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS).
Measure 4 g of curing agent.
Mix PDMS and curing agent vigorously using a spatula or pipette tip for 2-3 min.
Spin the tube at 100 x g for 2-3 min to remove large air bubbles.
Pour approximately 15-20 g of the mixture over the master wafer.
De-gas using a desiccator.
Incubate the assembly in an oven at 70 °C for at least 2 h.
Remove the PDMS block from the cooled master wafer carefully.
Cut individual PDMS blocks containing single microfluidic devices.
Place the PDMS block on a dark surface and adjust light direction to make channels visible.
Make holes in the inlets using biopsy punches of 0.5 mm diameter.
Make holes in the exit channel using biopsy punches of 3 mm diameter.
Gently push the biopsy punch through the PDMS block completely.
Retract the biopsy punch while rotating it in alternate directions to avoid cracks.
Take a transparent glass coverslip.
Pour approximately 0.5 mL of PDMS onto the center of the glass slide.
Gently tilt the glass slide to spread PDMS across, ensuring total coverage.
Mount the glass slide on the spin coater centrally.
Spin the glass slide at 500 rpm for 15 seconds (incrementing by 100 rpm/s).
Increase speed and spin at 1,000 rpm for 30 seconds (incrementing by 500 rpm/s).
Place the PDMS-coated glass slide coated side up on a raised platform in a covered Petri dish.
Bake the PDMS-coated glass slide at 70 °C for 2 hours.
Clean the PDMS block by sticking and removing scotch tape twice, keeping the cleaned side facing up.
Clean the PDMS-coated glass slide with pressurized air/N2 using a blow gun, keeping the clean side facing up.
Place the PDMS block engraved channels up and the PDMS-coated glass slide coated side up in the vacuum chamber of the plasma cleaner.
Switch on the vacuum.
Expose contents to air plasma at 12 MHz radio frequency for 15 seconds.
Place the PDMS-coated glass slide on a clean surface with the PDMS side facing upward.
Gently place the PDMS block with the microfluidic pattern toward the PDMS-coated glass slide, allowing them to bond.
Bake the bonded devices at 70 °C for 2 h.
Connect the pressure-driven flow controller to an external pressure source (up to 6 bars).
Calibrate the pressure pump according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Cut tubing into four equal-sized pieces approximately 20 cm in length.
Insert 23 G stainless steel 90° bent connectors at one end of each piece.
Insert the tubing into the microfluidic reservoir stand, sealing it with microfluidic fittings.
Ensure the tubing length allows contact with the bottom of the 1.5 mL reservoir tube.
Prepare a 5% (w/v) PVA solution by dissolving PVA powder in water at 80 °C for 3 hours with constant stirring.
Filter the prepared PVA solution before use.
Wait 2 hours after bonding and baking the microfluidic device before starting PVA treatment.
Dispense 200 µL of filtered 5% w/v PVA solution into a 1.5 mL tube.
Submerge one end of the tubing in the PVA solution and connect the other end to the inlet of the OA channel on the microfluidic device.
Repeat the above step without PVA (empty 1.5 mL tube).
Connect it to the LO and IA channels.
Increase the pressure of the OA phase to 100 mbar to flow the PVA solution in the OA channels.
Increase the pressures of the IA and LO phases to 120 mbar to prevent backflow of PVA solution inside these channels.
Adjust the pressures of individual channels if needed to keep the meniscus steady at the production junction.
Flow the PVA solution for approximately 5 min to ensure complete functionalization of the exit channel.
Detach the tubing from the OA inlet.
Immediately increase the pressure in the LO and IA channels to 2 bar.
Use a tubing connected to a negative pressure channel (−900 mbar) to remove excess PVA first from the exit channel and then from the OA inlet.
Bake the device at 120 °C for 15 min.
Let it cool down before use.
Store the device under ambient conditions for at least 1 month.
Dispense 76 μL of DOPC (25 mg/mL) into a round-bottom flask using a glass syringe.
Dispense 16.6 μL of Liss Rhod PE (1 mg/mL) into the same round-bottom flask using another glass syringe.
Use a compressed N2 blow gun to evaporate the chloroform and form a dried lipid film at the bottom of the flask.
Place the flask in the desiccator for at least 2 hours under continuous vacuum to remove any remaining chloroform.
Add 100 μL of ethanol into the round-bottom flask.
Gently pipette or shake the flask to ensure the lipids are dissolved and form a 10% (w/v) lipid stock solution.
Pipette the solution into a dark glass vial.
Gently flush the vial with nitrogen using a blow gun to replace the air with an inert atmosphere.
Seal the lid of the vial with paraffin film.
Store the vial at -20°C.
Prepare a 20 mM dextran solution with a molecular weight of 6,000.
Prepare a 60% v/v glycerol stock solution.
Prepare a buffer of choice, such as 5x phosphate-buffered saline (pH 7.4).
Cut out a small slanted piece at the end of the pipette tip for effective pipetting of pure glycerol.
Pipette 100 µL of IA solution, including yellow fluorescent protein (YFP) and other components as specified.
Prepare 100 µL of OA solution with 5% F68 surfactant and PBS.
Prepare 100 µL of ES solution with PBS.
Check the osmotic balance between the IA and OA solutions to prevent liposome bursting or shrinking during production.
Mix 4 µL of stock lipid into 76 µL of 1-octanol to prepare the LO phase, resulting in a final DOPC concentration of 5 mg/mL.
Centrifuge the samples at 700 x g for 60 s.
Dispense solutions IA, LO, and OA into three 1.5 mL tubes.
Assemble the tubes as mentioned in step 5.1.
Connect the assembled tubes to the PVA-treated microfluidic chip (step 5.2.6).
Apply a positive pressure of ~100 mbar on the IA channel.
Apply a positive pressure of ~100 mbar on the LO channel.
Apply a positive pressure of ~200 mbar on the OA channel.
Decrease the OA pressure to 100 mbar.
Increase the LO pressure to 200 mbar.
Adjust the LO pressure to 100 mbar once air bubbles are dispensed into the EW.
Increase the IA pressure to 200 mbar.
Wait until all air in the IA channel is removed.
Pipette 10 µL of ES into the exit chamber.
Put a cover slide on the exit hole to avoid evaporation.
Gradually increase the LO pressure in 1 mbar increments if the LO is pushed back.
Ensure double emulsion production begins once all three phases start co-flowing at the junction.
Adjust pressures gradually (steps of 0.1-1 mbar) based on quality of double emulsion production.
Check that double-emulsion droplets flow downstream to EW.
Ensure octanol pockets become more prominent as droplets move.
Confirm that octanol pockets are pinched off, forming liposomes.
Ensure the post-production channel is long enough for production.
Verify that migration of double emulsions is slow enough for dewetting.
